newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Bomb kills three, wounds six on Russian train.
newsitem.headline: Bomb kills three, wounds six on Russian train.

text.p: A bomb went off on a train travelling between Moscow and St Petersburg on Friday, killing three people and wounding six, an emergencies ministry official said.
"It was a bomb which was hidden in the toilets of one of the carriages," a duty officer told Reuters, adding that the incident happened at around 6:30 p.m. (1430 GMT).
He said the train, heading for St Petersburg, was near Torbino station in the Novgorod region northwest of Moscow when the blast occurred.
"After a short delay, traffic on the line resumed," another emergencies ministry official said by telephone. He did not make clear whether the damaged train continued on its journey or not.
The officials said they had no indication yet as to who might have planted the bomb.
Bomb blasts are a fairly common occurance in Russia, where explosives are often used in contract killings of businessmen.
Earlier this year, four people were killed when blasts ripped through two stations in southern Russia.
Moscow blamed those explosions on Chechen rebels, but separatist leaders in the southern republic, torn by a conflict with Russian troops which ended last August, denied any involvment.
